translationRepairs: Yan Zhenqing was a investigating censor; when he was sent to Longyou, Han once gave a banquet, and Zhenqing said to Han, "Your Excellency went from commandant to general and straightway rose to a frontier command—youth can be feared; are there not men [among them]?"

Yan Zhenqing was an investigating censor; when he was sent to Longyou, Han once gave a banquet, and Zhenqing said to Han, "Your Excellency went from commandant to general and straightway rose to a frontier command—youth can be feared; are there not men [among them]?"
Literal English uses the ungrammatical article 'a investigating'; the office 監察御史 requires 'an investigating censor'.
if respectfully he can enter the city, then the hearts of ten thousand men will be made firm.
if he succeeds in entering the city, then the hearts of ten thousand men will be made firm.
敬得入城 is concessive success in entering, not a manner adverb 'respectfully'; the idiomatic already translates the sense as reaching the city.

On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, Shi Siming marched from Fanyang to relieve the siege. The armies clashed north of Anyang on the Yellow River. The imperial side faltered; Jiong took an arrow wound and withdrew.

On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, Shi Siming marched from Fanyang to relieve the siege. The armies clashed north of the Anyang River. The imperial side faltered; Jiong took an arrow wound and withdrew.
安陽河北 is the north bank of the Anyang River, not Anyang on the Yellow River; 河 here names 安陽河.

On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, the rebel general Shi Siming came from Fanyang to relieve the city; they fought north of Anyang on the Yellow River; the imperial army was at a disadvantage; Jiong was struck by an arrow and fled.

On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, the rebel general Shi Siming came from Fanyang to relieve the city; they fought north of the Anyang River; the imperial army was at a disadvantage; Jiong was struck by an arrow and fled.
Same error as the idiomatic: 安陽河北 is not the Yellow River.
In the seventh month of Baoying 762 an edict declared: "The former Governor of Xiangzhou, Pei Ying, is coarse by nature and reckless in conduct.
In the seventh month of Baoying 1 (AD 762), an edict declared: "The former Governor of Xiangzhou, Pei Ying, is coarse by nature and reckless in conduct.
寶應元年 is Baoying 1, corresponding to AD 762. The revision restores the source reign-year while retaining the useful Western conversion.
He may be made Grand General with the insignia of a chief minister, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Qi, with an estate of two hundred households, and also Governor of Jingzhao.",

He may be granted the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Equal in Ceremonial Standing to the Three Excellencies), concurrently serve as Censor-in-Chief, be enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with a substantive fief of two hundred households, and also serve as Governor of Jingzhao."
The proposal correctly removes the stray punctuation, but 開府儀同三司 is a court rank, not "Grand General with the insignia of a chief minister." The revision fixes both problems.
In the first year of Qianyuan, He was summoned to serve as Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
In the first year of Qianyuan, he was summoned to serve as Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
Mid-sentence 'He' is an ungrammatical capital after a comma.
On the thirteenth of the fourth month of Qianyuan 760, Xiangzhou officers Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie mutinied and killed Prefect Shi Hui.
On the thirteenth day of the fourth month of Qianyuan 3 (AD 760), Xiangzhou officers Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie mutinied and killed Prefect Shi Hui.
乾元三年 is Qianyuan 3, corresponding to AD 760. The revision preserves both dating systems without presenting 760 as a reign year.

Zhen was made Governor of Xiangzhou, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan East military governor and disposal commissioner over ten prefectures: Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Jin, Shang, Sui, Ying, Fu, and Fu,

Zhen was made Governor of Xiangzhou, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan East military governor and disposal commissioner over ten prefectures: Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Jin, Shang, Sui, Ying, and Fu,
The literal doubles the last prefecture 'Fu' after 復; the Chinese list does not repeat it.
When troops finally marched, Zhongsheng was already dead.
When the troops finally marched, Zhongsheng had already fallen into rebel hands.
Later context proves 沒 means that Zhongsheng was lost to or captured by the rebels, not killed. The revision states that naturally without a parenthetical gloss.
By the time the army went out, Zhongsheng had already perished.
By the time the army went out, Zhongsheng had already been captured by the rebels.
Later context proves 沒 refers to capture rather than death; the literal field should state the implied enemy context directly.

The eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen then dominated court. He claimed Zhen's words smacked of treason; Wang Zhongsheng, returning after the rebellion, was made to testify that Zhen had colluded with the enemy, and Yuanzhen kept him in rebel hands for three years.

The eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen then dominated the court. He claimed that Zhen's words smacked of treason; after the rebels were pacified, Wang Zhongsheng returned and testified that Zhen had colluded with them and had deliberately left him in rebel hands for three years.
故令仲昇陷賊三年 belongs to Zhongsheng's accusation against Lai Zhen, not to an action by Cheng Yuanzhen. The revision makes both the speaker and pronoun referents explicit.
Collator Yin Liang came afterward and wept alone by the body; he sold his donkey for coffin and shroud, then at night persuaded Magistrate Sun Yan, who consented out of duty.
Collator Yin Liang came afterward and wept alone by the body; he sold his donkey for coffin and shroud, then at night persuaded Magistrate Changsun Yan, who consented out of duty.
長孫 is the compound surname Changsun, not Sun; 長孫演 is Changsun Yan.

The collator Yin Liang arrived later; he alone wept beside the corpse; he sold the donkey he rode to provide coffin and shroud; at night he went to the county magistrate Sun Yan and told him the story; Yan was moved by righteousness and agreed.

The collator Yin Liang arrived later; he alone wept beside the corpse; he sold the donkey he rode to provide coffin and shroud; at night he went to the county magistrate Changsun Yan and told him the story; Yan was moved by righteousness and agreed.
Same surname error: 長孫演 is Changsun Yan, not Sun Yan.
In Guangde 763 his rank and fief were posthumously restored.
In Guangde 1 (AD 763), his rank and fief were posthumously restored.
廣德元年 is Guangde 1, corresponding to AD 763. The revision retains the Western date while restoring the source reign-year.

In the first year of Yongtai, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, and allied tribes—more than a hundred thousand—raided Fengtian and Liquan. Zhiguang met them at Chengcheng, took vast booty, and chased them to Binzhou.

In the first year of Yongtai, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, and allied tribes—more than a hundred thousand—raided Fengtian and Liquan. Zhiguang met them at Chengcheng, took vast booty, and chased them to Fuzhou.
鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Binzhou (邠州).

In the first year of Yongtai, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, Qi, Hun, and Nulaci—more than a hundred thousand in all—raided Fengtian, Liquan, and other counties; Zhiguang intercepted them and broke them at Chengcheng, seized camels, horses, and military stores by the tens of thousands, and pursued the bandits to Binzhou.

In the first year of Yongtai, Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, Qi, Hun, and Nulaci—more than a hundred thousand in all—raided Fengtian, Liquan, and other counties; Zhiguang intercepted them and broke them at Chengcheng, seized camels, horses, and military stores by the tens of thousands, and pursued the bandits to Fuzhou.
Same 鄜州 / Binzhou error in the literal.
At odds with Du Mian, he killed Binzhou prefect Zhang Lin, slaughtered eighty-one of Mian's kin, and burned three thousand dwellings in Fangzhou.
At odds with Du Mian, he killed Fuzhou prefect Zhang Lin, slaughtered eighty-one of Mian's kin, and burned three thousand dwellings in Fangzhou.
鄜州刺史 is prefect of 鄜州 (Fuzhou), not Binzhou.
In the second year of Yongtai, in the twelfth month Zhiguang murdered former Guozhou prefect Sun Pangchong on his own authority.
In the twelfth month of Yongtai 2, Zhiguang on his own authority murdered Pang Chong, former Governor of Guozhou and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
The damaged string 兼御史中孫龐充 represents 兼御史中丞龐充: Pang Chong, concurrently Censor-in-Chief. The parallel annal in jiutangshu/011 also names the victim as 龐充.
The historiographer writes: I have read the biography of Li Ling—defeated, unable to die, he submitted to the barbarians; neither loyal subject nor filial son—and I have long sighed at it.

The historiographer writes: I have read the biography of Li Ling—defeated, unable to die, he submitted to the barbarians; he could be neither loyal minister to his lord nor filial son to his mother—and I have long sighed at it.
The Chinese 君不得為忠臣，母不得為孝子 names lord and mother; the idiomatic drops both referents.

The historiographer says—the historiographer says: I have read the biography of Li Ling; defeated in battle he could not die, bent his integrity and surrendered in the barbarians' court; the lord could not be a loyal minister, the mother could not be a filial son—I have long sighed over this.

The historiographer says: I have read the biography of Li Ling; defeated in battle he could not die, bent his integrity and surrendered in the barbarians' court; he could not be a loyal minister to his lord nor a filial son to his mother—I have long sighed over this.
史臣曰 is doubled in the source English, and 君/母 are inverted so that lord and mother become the subject of 忠臣/孝子.
That day Zhiguang was beheaded by a commander in his tent; his sons Yuanyao and Yuanqian and two others were brought in submission.
That day one of Zhiguang's subordinate commanders beheaded him and presented his head together with his two sons, Yuanyao and Yuanqian.
等二人 counts the two named sons rather than two additional people. The revision also makes clear what the commander presented.
